guia.what: An editable `<input>` with autocomplete (APG combobox pattern). You type to filter the list and pick an option, or—with `data-ts-allow-custom` on the root—keep a free-form value. Unlike the Select, the text field is the control.
whenUse: The list is long, and typing to filter is the natural way to reach an option.
The user might need a value that isn’t in the list (`data-ts-allow-custom`).
Autocompleting as they type saves more than opening a panel and scanning it.
You need to assign several values from a long or server-backed list, and it helps to see them in the field (`data-ts-multiple`).
whenAvoid: The list is short and known, so opening it and picking is enough → `select`.
You want a search box inside the panel, or to summarize several options as a count → `select`.
You’re not capturing a value but running app-wide commands → `command-palette`.
dos: Show a clear empty state when the filter finds nothing.
If you allow free-form values, make it obvious how to confirm a new one.
donts: Don’t use it for four options. For so few, the input adds more friction than a Select.
Don’t hide important options behind the filter without a visible default.

teclado.action: Selects the focused option, or confirms the typed text.
Reverts to the previous value and closes.
Adds or removes the focused option without closing the panel. With no focused option, adds the typed text if it matches an option or free-form values are allowed.
With an empty field, removes the last tag. With text, deletes text.
Moves through each tag’s remove button before reaching the field.

nucleo: It’s a free-text field with live filtering and a list of options. The APG combobox pattern on top of Select’s list, plus filtering as you type. Esc with the panel open doesn’t propagate to a Popover that contains it, and hovering an option makes it active. Groups (`role="group"` with `aria-labelledby`) are filtered by hiding the heading of any group left empty.
